name: Phase3 Workflow
raw_input: Checkout Revamp Initiative. Customers abandon cart when shipping estimates are unclear. We must show delivery dates before payment within 200ms P95. Security: PCI scope must not store raw card data. OTP login via SMS for B2B portal. Integrate Stripe Premium tier. Support 10k concurrent sessions, p99 < 500ms, GDPR deletion within 30 days.

source_clauses.text: Customers abandon cart when shipping estimates are unclear.
We must show delivery dates before payment within 200ms P95.
Security: PCI scope must not store raw card data.
OTP login via SMS for B2B portal.
Support 10k concurrent sessions, p99 < 500ms, GDPR deletion within 30 days.

requirement_brief.cleaned_summary: The checkout flow will be revamped to include upfront delivery date estimates and integrate Stripe Premium payments while ensuring PCI compliance by avoiding storage of raw card data. An SMS-based OTP login mechanism will be added for the B2B portal. The platform must support 10,000 concurrent sessions with a p99 response time under 500 ms and guarantee GDPR-compliant data deletion within 30 days. Delivery date estimates must render in under 200 ms at the 95th percentile.

summary.title: Checkout Revamp
summary.one_liner: Faster, clearer, and fully compliant checkout and login experiences.
summary.objective: Increase conversion and trust by showing upfront delivery dates, offering premium payment processing, and simplifying B2B access while guaranteeing enterprise-grade performance and privacy compliance.
in_scope: SMS-based OTP Login for B2B Portal

architecture_brief.overview: Micro-service oriented checkout stack running in AWS eu-west-1. A React SPA and B2B Next.js portal invoke Delivery-Estimate, Payment-Proxy, Order, Auth and User services exposed through an API Gateway. Stripe Checkout handles payment UI to keep us out of PCI scope; Twilio delivers OTP codes. Redis fronts the Delivery-Estimate service to stay ≤200 ms P95, while Aurora Postgres stores canonical order, user and audit data. All services run containerised on ECS Fargate with autoscaling to 10 k concurrent sessions.

apis.description: Return delivery date estimate for SKU + destination. Response ≤200 ms P95.
Create Stripe PaymentIntent and associate cart + delivery estimate.
Finalize order once Stripe webhook confirms payment.
Send SMS OTP to B2B user phone.
Verify OTP and return JWT access token.
GDPR delete request. Triggers 30-day deletion workflow.

non_functional_requirements: Performance: ≤200 ms P95 for /delivery-estimate, ≤500 ms P99 overall
Scalability: 10 k concurrent sessions; autoscale services on CPU/RPS
Security: No raw card data stored (PCI SAQ-A), TLS 1.2+, JWT signed with RS256
Privacy: GDPR delete executed within 30 days, data encrypted at rest (AES-256)
Observability: 99 % of requests traced, error budget alarms
Compliance: PCI-DSS SAQ-A, GDPR Article 17 support

decisions.decision: Use Stripe Checkout & PaymentElement instead of custom card forms.
decisions.rationale: Keeps us in SAQ-A scope; avoids handling cardholder data.
decisions.trade_offs: Less control over UI; dependency on Stripe availability.

decisions.decision: Cache delivery estimates in Redis with 5-minute TTL.
decisions.rationale: Guarantees ≤200 ms P95 even under high load.
decisions.trade_offs: Potential staleness; need cache-invalidation strategy when carrier SLAs change.

decisions.decision: Adopt JWT stateless sessions for B2B portal.
decisions.rationale: Horizontal scalability and no server-side session storage.
decisions.trade_offs: Requires robust token revocation strategy for compromised accounts.

decisions.decision: Run services on ECS Fargate rather than Kubernetes.
decisions.rationale: Reduced ops overhead, fast scaling, fits team skillset.
decisions.trade_offs: Less flexibility for custom scheduling; vendor lock-in.

architecture_brief.deployment: All services containerised and deployed on AWS ECS Fargate in eu-west-1 across 3 AZs; frontends served via CloudFront + S3. API Gateway fronts public APIs with WAF. Aurora Postgres in Multi-AZ with autoscaling writers/readers. ElastiCache Redis cluster in cluster-mode for high throughput. Auto-scaling policies on CPU and RPS enable 10 k concurrent sessions. CI/CD via GitHub Actions → ECR → ECS rolling deployments with one-minute health checks.

stories.title: Show delivery date estimate before payment within 200 ms (P95)
stories.goal: know the expected delivery date before committing to payment
stories.benefit: gain confidence and reduce cart abandonment
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer has items in the cart, when they reach the shipping step of checkout, then the system displays an accurate delivery date estimate before the payment section appears.
The system shall return the delivery-date estimate in ≤200 ms for at least 95% of requests measured over any 1-hour window.
If inventory or carrier data is unavailable, the system shall display “Estimate unavailable—check again later” without blocking checkout.
Delivery estimates shall update automatically when the customer changes shipping address or speed.

stories.title: Process payments via Stripe Premium without storing raw card data
stories.goal: pay for an order securely and reliably
stories.benefit: complete purchase with confidence that card data is protected
acceptance_criteria: The system shall tokenize card details directly with Stripe Premium using client-side elements, ensuring no raw card data touches the platform’s servers.
Given a valid payment token, when the customer confirms payment, then the system records a successful transaction and progresses the order status to 'Paid'.
Given a declined or failed tokenization/payment, when the customer attempts payment, then the system surfaces Stripe’s error message and allows retry.
PCI-DSS scans confirm zero raw PAN or CVV data stored in application logs, databases, or memory snapshots.

stories.title: Enable SMS-based OTP login for B2B portal
stories.goal: log in quickly without remembering a password
stories.benefit: gain secure access to the portal with minimal friction
acceptance_criteria: Given a registered phone number, when a B2B user requests login, then the system sends a one-time password via the SMS Gateway.
Given the user enters the correct OTP within 5 minutes, then the system grants an authenticated session.
If an incorrect OTP is entered three times, the system shall lock the login attempt for 10 minutes and display an error.
OTP codes shall be single-use and automatically expire after the 5-minute window.

stories.title: Support 10 k concurrent sessions with p99 response time <500 ms
stories.goal: assure the platform scales under peak traffic
stories.benefit: maintain fast, reliable service during high demand
acceptance_criteria: Load tests simulating 10,000 concurrent authenticated sessions shall complete with overall p99 response time <500 ms for all endpoints, including checkout and OTP flows.
No error rate above 0.1% shall be observed during the load test window.
Auto-scaling events shall not cause response times to exceed the 500 ms p99 threshold.

stories.title: Fulfill GDPR data-erasure requests within 30 days
stories.goal: ensure personal data is deleted promptly upon request
stories.benefit: maintain regulatory compliance and user trust
acceptance_criteria: Given a verified erasure request, when the request is submitted, then the system schedules deletion of all personal data tied to the user within 30 days.
Upon completion of deletion, the system shall send an audit log entry and a confirmation notification to the requestor.
Any attempt to access deleted user data after completion shall return 'User Not Found'.
Automated nightly jobs shall report any pending deletions older than 25 days for manual review.

test_cases.title: Customer sees delivery estimate within 200 ms at shipping step
test_cases.given: Given a logged-in customer has items in the cart and reaches the shipping step of checkout
test_cases.when: When the page requests a delivery-date estimate for the selected address and shipping speed
test_cases.then: Then the system returns an accurate delivery-date estimate in ≤200 ms and displays it before the payment section appears

test_cases.title: Inventory or carrier data unavailable shows fallback message
test_cases.given: Given carrier API is unreachable or inventory service times out
test_cases.when: When the customer reaches the shipping step
test_cases.then: Then the system displays “Estimate unavailable—check again later” without blocking checkout flow

test_cases.title: Rapid address change updates estimate and meets P95 latency
test_cases.given: Given a customer rapidly toggles between two different shipping addresses/speeds 100 times within a minute
test_cases.when: When each estimate is requested
test_cases.then: Then 95% of the 100 requests complete in ≤200 ms and each displayed estimate matches the latest selected address/speed

test_cases.title: Unauthorized user cannot query delivery estimates for another cart
test_cases.given: Given an unauthenticated or differently authenticated user crafts an API call referencing another customer’s cart ID
test_cases.when: When the request for a delivery-date estimate is sent
test_cases.then: Then the system returns HTTP 401/403 without revealing any delivery or inventory data

test_cases.title: Successful Stripe token payment marks order as Paid
test_cases.given: Given the client obtains a valid Stripe Premium payment token for the customer’s card
test_cases.when: When the customer confirms payment with that token
test_cases.then: Then the platform creates a charge via Stripe, records the transaction, and updates order status to “Paid”

test_cases.title: Declined payment surfaces Stripe error and allows retry
test_cases.given: Given Stripe responds with a declined_card error for the token
test_cases.when: When the customer attempts to pay
test_cases.then: Then the system shows the exact Stripe error message, leaves order in “Payment Pending”, and allows another attempt

test_cases.title: Double-click payment button charges only once
test_cases.given: Given a customer double-clicks the Pay button causing two nearly simultaneous submissions with the same token
test_cases.when: When the backend processes the requests
test_cases.then: Then only one successful charge is created and the second response returns idempotency acknowledgement without duplicate billing

test_cases.title: No raw PAN or CVV stored or logged
test_cases.given: Given a PCI-DSS forensic scan of databases, logs, and memory after 10k payment attempts
test_cases.when: When the scan searches for PAN or CVV patterns
test_cases.then: Then zero instances of raw card data are found on the platform’s infrastructure

test_cases.title: Correct OTP within 5 minutes grants session
test_cases.given: Given a registered phone number requests login and receives an OTP via SMS
test_cases.when: When the user enters the correct OTP within 5 minutes
test_cases.then: Then the system authenticates the user and starts an authenticated session

test_cases.title: Three wrong OTP attempts lock login for 10 minutes
test_cases.given: Given the user enters an incorrect OTP three times in a row
test_cases.when: When the third incorrect entry is submitted
test_cases.then: Then the system locks further attempts for 10 minutes and shows an error message

test_cases.title: OTP expires exactly at 5-minute boundary and is single-use
test_cases.given: Given an OTP generated at T0
test_cases.when: When the same OTP is submitted once at T0+5 min−1 sec (accepted) and again at T0+5 min (boundary)
test_cases.then: Then the first submission succeeds and the second is rejected as expired or already used

test_cases.title: Rate-limit prevents OTP brute-force across numbers
test_cases.given: Given an attacker sends OTP verify requests with random codes for 50 phone numbers within 1 minute
test_cases.when: When the request volume exceeds the configured threshold
test_cases.then: Then the system throttles responses, logs the abuse, and does not reveal whether numbers are registered

test_cases.title: 10 k concurrent sessions meet p99 <500 ms and error rate <0.1%
test_cases.given: Given a load test simulating 10,000 authenticated sessions across all critical endpoints
test_cases.when: When the test runs for the defined peak window
test_cases.then: Then measured p99 response time is <500 ms and overall error rate is <0.1%

test_cases.title: Auto-scaling delay causing p99 breach fails test
test_cases.given: Given auto-scaling is intentionally slowed by 2 minutes during a repeat of the load test
test_cases.when: When traffic spikes to 10 k sessions
test_cases.then: Then p99 response time exceeds 500 ms and the test records failure as per SLA

test_cases.title: 10,001 concurrent sessions still maintain SLA margin
test_cases.given: Given a load test with 10,001 concurrent authenticated sessions (boundary +1)
test_cases.when: When all endpoints are exercised
test_cases.then: Then p99 response time remains ≤500 ms or the single additional session is gracefully queued without error

test_cases.title: DoS spike of unauthenticated traffic does not degrade authenticated p99
test_cases.given: Given 20,000 unauthenticated requests per second flood the public endpoints while 10,000 valid sessions remain active
test_cases.when: When the platform mitigates via rate-limiting and WAF
test_cases.then: Then authenticated traffic still meets p99 <500 ms and error rate <0.1%

test_cases.title: Verified erasure request schedules and completes within 30 days
test_cases.given: Given a Data Protection Officer submits a verified data-erasure request for user U on Day 0
test_cases.when: When the system processes scheduled deletion jobs
test_cases.then: Then all personal data for user U is deleted by Day 30, an audit log entry is created, and a confirmation notification is sent

test_cases.title: Unverified erasure request is rejected
test_cases.given: Given an erasure request is submitted without proper identity verification
test_cases.when: When the system validates the request
test_cases.then: Then the request is rejected with a verification required error and no deletion task is scheduled

test_cases.title: Pending deletions older than 25 days trigger nightly alert
test_cases.given: Given a deletion task for user U has been pending for 26 days
test_cases.when: When the automated nightly reporting job runs
test_cases.then: Then the task appears in the report for manual review

test_cases.title: Unauthorized user cannot erase another user’s data
test_cases.given: Given an authenticated user A attempts to submit an erasure request for user B’s account
test_cases.when: When the system processes the request
test_cases.then: Then the system returns HTTP 403 and logs the incident without scheduling deletion

risks.title: Delivery-date SLA may exceed 200ms P95
risks.description: Calculating and rendering delivery dates requires live calls to shipping-rate and inventory services. Without dedicated caching and parallelization, the new checkout path is unlikely to meet the 200 ms P95 budget, directly impacting cart conversion.
risks.mitigation: Begin this sprint by setting up a synthetic benchmark for the full delivery-date call chain, add in-memory/L2 cache for static carrier data, and profile query hotspots before feature freeze.

risks.title: Checkout path untested for 10k concurrent sessions, p99 < 500 ms
risks.description: The revamp introduces new DB queries and third-party calls. If connection pools, thread pools, and autoscaling policies are not tuned, latency will spike past the 500 ms p99 requirement under peak load, causing timeouts and lost revenue.
risks.mitigation: Add a Gatling/K6 load test that simulates 10k concurrent sessions this sprint, profile the bottlenecks, and set autoscaling thresholds plus DB pool limits based on the results.

risks.title: Accidental storage of raw card data violates PCI scope
risks.description: New logging in the checkout flow and Stripe integration could capture PAN or CVV in application logs, analytics events, or DB snapshots, expanding PCI scope and creating a breach vector.
risks.mitigation: Introduce a logging filter this sprint that redacts card fields, run a secrets-scanner over existing logs, and add an automated test that fails the build if raw card patterns are detected.

risks.title: OTP login via SMS lacks rate-limiting and fallback
risks.description: Brute-force OTP attempts or SMS delivery outages can lock out legitimate B2B users or allow account takeover, leading to incident response and support escalations.
risks.mitigation: Implement per-user/IP rate limiting and a maximum retry counter this sprint; add email-based OTP as a fallback path and monitor SMS provider delivery metrics.

risks.title: Single-point dependency on Stripe Premium API
risks.description: Checkout now relies solely on Stripe Premium endpoints; any API degradation or quota issue will block payments and expose us to downtime outside our control.
risks.mitigation: Add a circuit breaker with automatic downgrade to the existing Standard tier endpoints this sprint, and publish Prometheus alerts on Stripe latency/error rates.

risks.title: GDPR deletion SLA (30 days) not enforced across caches & backups
risks.description: User data removed from primary DB may still reside in read replicas, Redis caches, and object-store backups, breaching the 30-day GDPR requirement and risking fines.
risks.mitigation: Create a data-map this sprint that lists every store containing PII, add TTLs or scheduled purge jobs for each, and validate with an integration test that deletes propagate within 24 h.

auto_sprint_plan.requirement: Checkout Revamp Initiative. Customers abandon cart when shipping estimates are unclear. We must show delivery dates before payment within 200ms P95. Security: PCI scope must not store raw card data. OTP login via SMS for B2B portal. Integrate Stripe Premium tier. Support 10k concurrent sessions, p99 < 500ms, GDPR deletion within 30 days.

reviews.summary: The requirement mixes multiple initiatives and gives clear latency targets but lacks detailed scope, making clarity moderate.

stories.title: Customer sees delivery date estimate pre-payment
acceptance_criteria: Given a filled cart with valid shipping address, when the customer proceeds to the checkout page, then an estimated delivery date is displayed before any payment details are requested.
The delivery-date component must render with P95 <= 200 ms for the API call that supplies the estimate, measured under a load of 10 k concurrent sessions.
If the shipping service is unreachable, the UI must show a graceful fallback message (‘Delivery estimate unavailable’) and log the error.
Estimates must reflect the shipping method the customer selects (standard, expedited, etc.).
Unit and integration tests cover at least the top three shipping methods for the five primary regions we serve.

stories.title: Platform performance under peak load
acceptance_criteria: Under 10 000 concurrent authenticated sessions, overall page response time (TTFB) for checkout flow is < 500 ms at the 99th percentile.
Load tests are executed in a staging environment that mirrors production hardware and network configuration.
Results are published to the performance dashboard and reviewed by the SRE team before go-live.
Any regression above 10 % of the threshold blocks release.

stories.title: Stripe Premium payment processing
acceptance_criteria: Stripe Premium account is configured in test and production with correct API keys managed via secret vault.
The checkout flow successfully creates PaymentIntents via Stripe API and receives confirmation callbacks.
All mandatory Premium-tier features (Radar fraud signals, advanced dispute data) are enabled and surfaced in our admin portal.
Rollback plan exists to switch to current payment provider within 30 minutes if Stripe is unavailable.
End-to-end payment test transactions (Visa, Mastercard, Amex) pass in test and live modes.

stories.title: PCI scope exclusion: never store raw card data
acceptance_criteria: No service, log, or database table stores PAN, CVV, or magnetic-strip data in plain text or encrypted form.
Card data is tokenized client-side via Stripe Elements or equivalent and only tokens reach our backend.
Static code analysis and secret-scan pipelines fail the build if card patterns are detected.
Quarterly external PCI audit confirms zero storage of raw card data.

stories.title: SMS OTP login for B2B portal
acceptance_criteria: User enters company email, receives a 6-digit OTP via SMS to their registered phone number.
OTP is valid for 5 minutes and for a single use; expired or reused codes are rejected.
Rate limiting: max 3 OTP requests per user per 10 minutes; excess attempts return HTTP 429.
Successful OTP authentication issues a JWT valid for the session policy of the portal.
Audit logs capture OTP send, verification success/failure, and are retained per security policy.

stories.title: GDPR right-to-erasure within 30 days
acceptance_criteria: When a data-deletion request is received, all personally identifiable information for that user is removed or anonymized in production and backups within 30 calendar days.
Process is automated and exposes a progress API for compliance reporting.
Deletion jobs are idempotent and logged; failures trigger alerting within 1 hour.
Quarterly audit demonstrates 100 % compliance with the 30-day SLA.

concerns: No definition of which markets or shipping carriers are in scope for delivery-date estimates.
200 ms P95 requirement omits load pattern details (e.g., peak hour profiles) and measurement method.
Stripe Premium ‘integration’ is broad—unclear which features are mandatory and how success is measured beyond basic payment flow.
PCI clause asserts a rule but omits validation approach and scope of third-party tools.
OTP login does not specify SMS provider, fallback for delivery failures, or accessibility considerations.
GDPR deletion process does not define data categories, archival constraints, or responsibility assignment.
Concurrency requirement (10 k sessions) lacks environment specs (geo distribution, device mix) and whether read-only or transactional load.

reviews.summary: Implementable but requires a new Shipping Estimator microservice, SMS OTP flow, and Stripe migration while meeting strict latency/concurrency and PCI/GDPR constraints.

scenarios.title: Display delivery date before payment when items are in cart
scenarios.description: Verify that the checkout flow surfaces a delivery-date estimate on the payment page load for a standard logged-in customer.

scenarios.title: Delivery date API response time ≤200 ms at P95
scenarios.description: Load-test the shipping-estimate service with realistic mix to confirm 95th-percentile latency does not exceed 200 ms.

scenarios.title: Delivery date still visible when cart contents change
scenarios.description: Add/remove items during checkout and ensure delivery dates refresh appropriately without exceeding latency SLA.

scenarios.title: No raw card data stored in any system components
scenarios.description: Conduct static code analysis, DB scans and packet captures to ensure PAN, CVV, and expiry are never persisted or logged (PCI DSS).

scenarios.title: Stripe Premium payment succeeds with tokenized card info
scenarios.description: Complete a purchase through Stripe Premium tier using tokenization and confirm order creation, payment capture, and no card data storage.

scenarios.title: Stripe webhook failure and retry logic
scenarios.description: Simulate 500 errors and network timeouts on Stripe webhooks and verify exponential back-off and eventual consistency of payment status.

scenarios.title: OTP login via SMS happy path
scenarios.description: Request OTP, receive SMS, enter code, and gain access to B2B portal within validity window.

scenarios.title: OTP expiration and retry
scenarios.description: Attempt login with expired OTP and verify proper error messaging and ability to request a new code with rate limiting.

scenarios.title: Concurrent sessions 10k, p99 <500 ms across entire checkout
scenarios.description: Stress test full checkout flow (browse→cart→shipping→payment) with 10,000 simultaneous users and validate 99th percentile response time.

scenarios.title: GDPR Right-to-erasure processed within 30 days
scenarios.description: Submit deletion request and ensure all personal data (orders, payment tokens, SMS logs) are purged or anonymized inside 30 days.

scenarios.title: Accessibility of delivery-date component
scenarios.description: Use screen readers and keyboard navigation to confirm delivery-date text is announced and reachable.

scenarios.title: High-latency SMS gateway impact on OTP flow
scenarios.description: Inject 5-10 s SMS delivery delay and ensure UI handles waiting state and code validity timers gracefully.

scenarios.title: Simulate malicious card data entry attempts
scenarios.description: Input XSS payloads or excessively long strings into payment fields and ensure data is sanitized and not echoed in responses or logs.

scenarios.title: Checkout flow when shipping estimate service is down
scenarios.description: Force 503 from shipping service and verify user messaging, retry behavior, and that payment cannot proceed without delivery date.

edge_cases: Cart with items shipping to multiple regions/time zones requiring different delivery dates.
User switches shipping address after seeing estimate; confirm new estimate under 200 ms.
Customer on 2G/slow network where 200 ms target is unrealistic—how handled?
Simultaneous OTP requests from same user/device leading to SMS collision or code mismatch.
Clock skew between client and server causing OTP to appear expired prematurely.
Stripe webhook sent twice (duplicate event IDs) and idempotency handling.
GDPR deletion request while an order is in fraud-review or chargeback workflow.
10k sessions during partial CDN outage—does p99 still hold?
Payment attempt with network drop after authorization but before confirmation page.
Accessibility for color-blind users when delivery date uses color cues.
concerns: No definition of measurement window, environment, or tooling for 200 ms P95 and p99 <500 ms targets.
Unclear which pages must display delivery date ('before payment' could be several steps).
Missing details on supported carriers, time-zone logic, and how cutoff times affect estimates.
PCI compliance clause lacks specific scope boundaries (e.g., logs, analytics).
GDPR deletion workflows and data mapping across integrated systems (Stripe, SMS provider) not provided.
OTP SMS provider SLA, resend limits, and localization rules unspecified.
Accessibility requirements limited—need WCAG level, language, formatting guidance.

reviews.summary: The requirement is directionally secure and compliant but needs stronger controls around PCI data flow, SMS OTP hardening, and GDPR deletion to avoid critical gaps.

security_concerns.title: Improper handling/logging of payment card data
security_concerns.description: Although clause_081084a5 says no raw card data will be stored, accidental logging of full PAN/CVV in application logs, error traces, or analytics can still occur, breaching PCI DSS and exposing sensitive data.
security_concerns.mitigation: Implement strict data-masking middleware, disable verbose logging on payment fields, scan logs for PAN patterns in CI/CD, and apply tokenization or Stripe Elements so card data never touches backend servers.

security_concerns.title: Weaknesses in SMS-based OTP authentication
security_concerns.description: SMS OTP is vulnerable to SIM-swap, SS7 attacks, and phishing. An attacker could hijack sessions or perform account takeovers in the B2B portal.
security_concerns.mitigation: Add rate-limiting (≤5 attempts/10 min/IP & phone), short OTP TTL (≤5 min), bind OTP to device/browser fingerprint, support stronger second factors (TOTP, WebAuthn) as an alternative, and monitor for anomalous login patterns.

security_concerns.title: Unverified Stripe webhooks and key exposure
security_concerns.description: Integrating Stripe Premium tier requires inbound webhooks; if signatures are not verified or keys are mishandled, attackers could spoof events or exfiltrate revenue data.
security_concerns.mitigation: Use Stripe-provided signing secrets, validate event signatures, rotate API keys regularly, store secrets in a vault (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault), and restrict outbound network access for egress filtering.

security_concerns.title: Race conditions & session fixation at 10k concurrent sessions
security_concerns.description: High concurrency can expose race conditions in cart or checkout flow enabling double-spend, lost updates, or session fixation attacks.
security_concerns.mitigation: Adopt atomic cart operations with optimistic locking, generate new session IDs post-authentication, and run concurrency stress tests focusing on authentication and payment paths.

security_concerns.title: Insufficient input validation on shipping estimator
security_concerns.description: To meet 200 ms P95 latency, engineers may skip validation, allowing malicious users to inject oversized or malformed addresses leading to service degradation or SSRF to shipping APIs.
security_concerns.mitigation: Apply strict schema validation (e.g., JSON Schema), set length limits on address fields, sanitize external API requests, and implement circuit breakers/throttling for estimator calls.

security_concerns.title: Denial-of-Service via OTP or shipping estimate endpoints
security_concerns.description: Automated abuse could flood OTP SMS or shipping-quote endpoints, exhausting SMS credits or degrading latency SLOs.
security_concerns.mitigation: Implement CAPTCHA or proof-of-work on high-risk endpoints, apply IP and device-based rate limits, and monitor for anomalous traffic spikes.

compliance_concerns.title: PCI DSS Scope Control
compliance_concerns.description: Handling payments with Stripe still places systems that touch card data in PCI scope; failure to segment environment or use SAQ-A could require full PCI audit.
compliance_concerns.mitigation: Use Stripe Elements/Checkout to keep card data exclusively in Stripe-hosted fields, maintain network segmentation, complete SAQ-A annually, and run quarterly ASV scans.

compliance_concerns.title: GDPR Right-to-Erasure Implementation
compliance_concerns.description: Clause_5c5afbda mandates deletion within 30 days, but no process is defined to propagate deletes to Stripe, logs, backups, and analytics.
compliance_concerns.mitigation: Implement a data-deletion orchestration service with audit logging, ensure backups are encrypted and have differential deletion or max 30-day retention, and sign a GDPR-compliant DPA with Stripe.

compliance_concerns.title: Data Residency & Cross-Border Transfers
compliance_concerns.description: Stripe may process data in the US; transferring EU customer data without SCCs could violate GDPR.
compliance_concerns.mitigation: Use Stripe’s EU-only data processing option or sign SCCs, update privacy notice, and document TIA (Transfer Impact Assessment).

compliance_concerns.title: Auditability for SOC 2 Availability & Security Trust Criteria
compliance_concerns.description: Performance SLOs (200 ms P95, 500 ms P99) and high concurrency must be monitored and logged; lack of evidence jeopardizes SOC 2 controls for availability.
compliance_concerns.mitigation: Implement centralized logging (e.g., ELK/Splunk), retain logs ≥1 year, configure real-time alerts on SLO breaches, and document incident response runbooks.

concerns: Accidental storage or logging of cardholder data breaks PCI compliance
SMS OTP susceptible to hijacking without additional protections
Lack of automated GDPR deletion across all data stores and backups

reviews.summary: Too many open questions on metrics, rollback, and third-party dependencies; I would not green-light without another iteration.

business_risks.title: Stripe Premium dependency
business_risks.description: Entire payment flow hinges on a 3rd-party service whose roadmap, pricing, and SLA we do not control; an outage or fee change directly impacts revenue and margins.

business_risks.title: Shipping ETA accuracy vs. performance
business_risks.description: Showing delivery dates in ≤200 ms may require caching or approximation; inaccurate ETAs can increase returns and erode trust, while missing the latency target negates the stated goal of reducing abandonment.

business_risks.title: SMS OTP reliability and cost
business_risks.description: SMS delivery success varies by carrier and geography; high per-message fees and potential SIM-swap fraud expose us to unexpected costs and security holes that could block B2B adoption.

business_risks.title: Scalability projection
business_risks.description: Assuming 10 k concurrent sessions may be optimistic or insufficient; under-estimating demand risks downtime during peak seasons, hurting conversion rates.

business_risks.title: GDPR non-compliance exposure
business_risks.description: Meeting the 30-day deletion SLA requires end-to-end data lineage across Stripe and SMS vendors; failure could result in regulatory fines.

missing_requirements.title: Success metrics / KPI baseline
missing_requirements.description: No target reduction in cart-abandonment or revenue lift is defined, so we can’t judge ROI or decide when the revamp is successful.

missing_requirements.title: Rollback and feature flag strategy
missing_requirements.description: No plan for reverting checkout changes if latency, fraud, or conversion issues appear in production.

missing_requirements.title: Operational ownership & on-call model
missing_requirements.description: It’s unclear which team owns 24/7 support, incident response, and SLA monitoring for the new checkout, OTP, and GDPR processes.

missing_requirements.title: Detailed non-functional requirements
missing_requirements.description: Uptime %, error budget, and monitoring/alerting thresholds are not specified beyond latency, leaving gaps in reliability expectations.

missing_requirements.title: Accessibility and localization
missing_requirements.description: No statement about WCAG compliance or multi-language support, both critical for global user adoption and legal compliance.

missing_requirements.title: Cost and margin impact analysis
missing_requirements.description: Budgetary implications of Stripe Premium fees and SMS OTP traffic are not addressed, risking unplanned OPEX increases.

missing_requirements.title: Data source contract for shipping ETA
missing_requirements.description: Requirement doesn’t specify where delivery data comes from or accuracy SLA with carriers.

concerns: What concrete cart-abandonment and revenue KPIs will define success?
How will we mitigate or roll back if Stripe or shipping-ETA latency misses targets?
Who owns production support costs and SLAs for SMS OTP, GDPR deletes, and checkout uptime?

epic.title: Checkout Revamp
epic.description: Increase conversion and trust by showing upfront delivery dates, offering premium payment processing, and simplifying B2B access while guaranteeing enterprise-grade performance and privacy compliance.
key_results: Ship 5 user stories with acceptance criteria green
Pass 20 test cases at ≥95% green rate

stories.title: Show delivery date estimate before payment within 200 ms (P95)
stories.goal: know the expected delivery date before committing to payment
stories.benefit: gain confidence and reduce cart abandonment
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer has items in the cart, when they reach the shipping step of checkout, then the system displays an accurate delivery date estimate before the payment section appears.
The system shall return the delivery-date estimate in ≤200 ms for at least 95% of requests measured over any 1-hour window.
If inventory or carrier data is unavailable, the system shall display “Estimate unavailable—check again later” without blocking checkout.
Delivery estimates shall update automatically when the customer changes shipping address or speed.

stories.title: Process payments via Stripe Premium without storing raw card data
stories.goal: pay for an order securely and reliably
stories.benefit: complete purchase with confidence that card data is protected
acceptance_criteria: The system shall tokenize card details directly with Stripe Premium using client-side elements, ensuring no raw card data touches the platform’s servers.
Given a valid payment token, when the customer confirms payment, then the system records a successful transaction and progresses the order status to 'Paid'.
Given a declined or failed tokenization/payment, when the customer attempts payment, then the system surfaces Stripe’s error message and allows retry.
PCI-DSS scans confirm zero raw PAN or CVV data stored in application logs, databases, or memory snapshots.

stories.title: Enable SMS-based OTP login for B2B portal
stories.goal: log in quickly without remembering a password
stories.benefit: gain secure access to the portal with minimal friction
acceptance_criteria: Given a registered phone number, when a B2B user requests login, then the system sends a one-time password via the SMS Gateway.
Given the user enters the correct OTP within 5 minutes, then the system grants an authenticated session.
If an incorrect OTP is entered three times, the system shall lock the login attempt for 10 minutes and display an error.
OTP codes shall be single-use and automatically expire after the 5-minute window.

stories.title: Support 10 k concurrent sessions with p99 response time <500 ms
stories.goal: assure the platform scales under peak traffic
stories.benefit: maintain fast, reliable service during high demand
acceptance_criteria: Load tests simulating 10,000 concurrent authenticated sessions shall complete with overall p99 response time <500 ms for all endpoints, including checkout and OTP flows.
No error rate above 0.1% shall be observed during the load test window.
Auto-scaling events shall not cause response times to exceed the 500 ms p99 threshold.

stories.title: Fulfill GDPR data-erasure requests within 30 days
stories.goal: ensure personal data is deleted promptly upon request
stories.benefit: maintain regulatory compliance and user trust
acceptance_criteria: Given a verified erasure request, when the request is submitted, then the system schedules deletion of all personal data tied to the user within 30 days.
Upon completion of deletion, the system shall send an audit log entry and a confirmation notification to the requestor.
Any attempt to access deleted user data after completion shall return 'User Not Found'.
Automated nightly jobs shall report any pending deletions older than 25 days for manual review.

generated_test_suite.title: Generated test suite
generated_test_suite.summary: 11 tests across 5 categories — functional=1, negative=2, boundary=1, security=4, regression=3

tests.title: Successful login with valid credentials
tests.given: a registered user with valid email and password
tests.then: they are authenticated and a JWT session is issued

groups.description: Wrong inputs, error states, conflicting data.

tests.title: Wrong credentials / OTP rejected
tests.when: they submit a wrong password or an incorrect OTP
tests.then: the API returns 401 and the failure is rate-limit counted

tests.title: Login with malformed body
tests.when: they POST a malformed payload to the login endpoint
tests.then: the API returns 400 with a list of validation errors

groups.description: Limits — empty, max length, off-by-one, edges.

tests.title: Password at minimum length boundary
tests.then: the request succeeds; an 11-char password is rejected

tests.title: SQL injection in login payload
tests.given: any string field on the endpoint
tests.when: the caller submits a SQLi payload (e.g. "' OR 1=1 --")
tests.then: the value is stored verbatim or rejected — never executed
tests.expected_result: Attack is blocked or neutralized; no data leak

tests.title: Authentication required to call login
tests.when: the caller hits the login endpoint
tests.then: the API returns 401 and does NOT leak data
tests.expected_result: Attack is blocked or neutralized; no data leak

tests.title: Rate limiting on login
tests.then: the API returns 429 with a Retry-After header
tests.expected_result: Attack is blocked or neutralized; no data leak

tests.title: Brute-force lockout
tests.when: submits 5 wrong passwords or OTPs in a row
tests.then: the account is locked for 15 minutes and a security event is logged
tests.expected_result: Attack is blocked or neutralized; no data leak

groups.description: Adjacent flows that must keep working.

tests.title: Pre-existing flows still work after login change
tests.given: the new login feature has shipped
tests.when: the standard smoke suite is run
tests.then: all previously-green tests continue to pass

tests.title: API backwards-compat
tests.given: the login change touches a public endpoint
tests.when: an old client (v1 contract) calls it
tests.then: the request still succeeds; no breaking field changes

tests.title: Existing sessions remain valid
tests.when: the login change is deployed mid-day
tests.then: sessions stay valid and no forced logout occurs
